predecessors.name: Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic
predecessors.text: the Muslim lands of the South Caucasus, proclaimed independent by the Azerbaijani National Council 'after the Transcaucasian federation fell' on 28 May 1918

successors.name: Azerbaijan Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: the republic 'occupied' by the Soviet 11th Army on 28 April 1920

ledger.x: 28 May 1918: the Azerbaijani National Council proclaims independence after the Transcaucasian federation falls.
15 September 1918: 'The Ottoman Army of Islam and its Azeri allies, led by Nuri Pasha, entered Baku on 15 September'; the republic's government makes it the capital.
September 1918: the capital moves from Ganja to Baku.
17 November 1918: Allied (British) troops arrive in Baku after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October) replaced the Turkish troops.
15 May 1919: the Mughan Soviet Republic is proclaimed in the Lankaran district after a pro-Bolshevik protest overthrew the Mughan administration on 25 April.
June 1919: Armenian troops under Drastamat Kanayan take Nakhichevan city and destroy the Republic of Aras; Azerbaijani and Ottoman troops retake it in July.
10 August 1919: ceasefire over Nakhichevan ('On 10 August 1919, a ceasefire was signed'); the dispute itself continued to 1920.
19 August 1919: 'British forces left' Baku, ending the Allied occupation that began on 17 November 1918.
28 April 1920: the republic ceases to exist, ending its contest with Armenia over Karabakh, Zangezur and Nakhichevan.
1920: page silent on the Mughan Soviet Republic's end; the dossier closes the contest at the republic's own end, 28 April 1920, as a bridging judgment.
28 April 1920: the Soviet 11th Army occupies the republic and it 'ceased to exist'.

wars.name: Armenian-Azerbaijani war (1918-1920)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive (30 March 1918 - 28 November 1920): 'Most of Zangezur gained by Soviet Armenia'; the Karabakh and Nakhichevan disputes settled for Soviet Azerbaijan.

wars.name: Soviet invasion of Azerbaijan (April 1920)
wars.outcome: The operation began on 25 April; on 27 April a Provisional Revolutionary Committee issued an ultimatum; the 11th Army occupied the republic on 28 April and it ceased to exist.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Armenia (Karabakh, Zangezur, Nakhichevan), Georgia (Balakan, Zaqatala, Qakh) and the North Caucasus (Derbent) were claims and contests; the page says the map of the republic does not show disputed territories.
